name: Heijo-kyo
description: Capital of Japan for most of the Nara period.

name: Kuni-kyo
description: Capital for 4 years during the reign of Emperor Shomu.

name: Naniwa-kyo
description: Capital for a year between 744-745

name: Heijo-kyo
description: Capital was moved back to Heijo-kyo after 5 years.

name: Nagaoka-kyo
description: Briefly capital for 10 years until frequent natural disasters forced the move to Heian-kyo

name: Heian-kyo
description: Imperial capital of Japan for over 1000 years until 1868

name: Kyoto
description: Imperial capital of Japan for over 1000 years until 1868

name: Tokyo
description: Capital of Japan since 1868

name: Kamakura
description: Shogunal capital from 1192 to 1333.

name: Edo
description: Shogunal capital from 1603 to 1868 when it was renamed to Tokyo.

name: Kyoto
description: Emperor Meiji moved east to Tokyo, the new 'Eastern Capital', in 1868, resulting in Kyoto losing its status as imperial capital after 1,074 years.

name: Asuka-kyo
description: Center of political power and early Buddhist culture during the Asuka period.

name: Fujiwara-kyo
description: First Japanese capital constructed using a Chinese-style grid layout.

name: Otsu-kyo
description: Brief capital established by Emperor Tenmu near Lake Biwa following administrative reforms.

name: Shigaraki-no-miya
description: Temporary capital under Emperor Shōmu during the construction of the Great Buddha.

name: Dazaifu
description: Military and diplomatic administrative capital overseeing foreign relations and Kyushu.

name: Hakata
description: Primary international port for trade with China and Korea; target of Mongol invasions.

name: Sakai
description: Autonomous merchant-governed port city famous for weapons, tea culture, and foreign trade.

name: Nagasaki
description: Sole legal window to Western trade (via Dutch Dejima) during the Sakoku period.

name: Osaka
description: Economic heart of feudal Japan, known as 'The Nation's Kitchen' (Tenka no Kkitchen).

name: Odawara
description: Impregnable stronghold of the Late Hōjō clan controlling the Kanto region.

name: Gifu
description: Oda Nobunaga's headquarters during his early unification campaigns.

name: Azuchi
description: De facto political center constructed by Oda Nobunaga before his betrayal at Honnō-ji.

name: Sendai
description: Castle town founded by Date Masamune, key regional power center of the Tohoku region.

name: Nagoya
description: Major castle town established by the Owari branch of the Tokugawa clan.

name: Kagoshima
description: Seat of the powerful Satsuma Domain and site of early European contacts.

name: Hagi
description: Capital of the Chōshū Domain, birthplace of many Meiji Restoration leaders.

name: Hirado
description: Early foreign trading post hosting Dutch, English, and Portuguese merchants.

name: Yokohama
description: First treaty port opened to Western trade following the arrival of Commodore Perry.

name: Sapporo
description: Administrative center built during the Meiji development of Hokkaido.
